messages:
sara.m: Heads up — onboarding a new private deployment customer (acme-privacy) tomorrow. Need a quick runbook: where do we expose Prometheus/Grafana for Private/VPC deployments? Do we give them a per-tenant Grafana URL or do we expect them to self-host and scrape? They also want to forward application logs via OTLP to our ingestion endpoint. Any short config snippets and network notes? cc @devon

devon: Two patterns we support:
1) Customer-managed observability (recommended for full isolation): we provide helm charts + example values so Prometheus/Grafana run inside their VPC/cluster.
2) Managed-per-tenant (we host a tenant-scoped Grafana/Prometheus behind the private console).
For acme-privacy I recommended pattern 1. Docs: https://internal.redwood.dev/private-observability

mike.r: Repo with charts and dashboards: git@github.com:redwood/platform-observability.git — dashboards under dashboards/. We keep tenant-specific dashboard JSON templates named dashboards/<tenant>-*.json.

devon: OTLP/log forwarding: we accept OTLP over HTTPS to our ingest endpoint. They must include the tenant header (X-Tenant-ID). Endpoint: https://ingest.private.redwood/api/v1/otlp/<tenant-id>
Example OTEL Collector snippet (HTTP exporter):
```
exporters:
  otlphttp:
    endpoint: https://ingest.private.redwood/api/v1/otlp
    headers:
      "X-Tenant-ID": "acme-privacy"
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      exporters: [otlphttp]
```

alex.p: Prometheus options: if we deploy Prometheus in their cluster we provide scrape configs. If they self-host Prometheus and want us to scrape (less common), they must expose scrape targets over the private peering and whitelist our control-plane IPs. Example scrape relabel for tenant pods:
```
- job_name: 'redwood-tenant'
  kubernetes_sd_configs:
  - role: pod
  relabel_configs:
  - source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_namespace]
    regex: 'redwood-.*'
    action: keep
```

sara.m: Got it. They already asked about alert noise — noisy latency alerts from last week. Quick advice for tuning?

mike.r: Alerts live in alerts/tenant-rules.yaml in the repo. For latency alerts we generally: increase `for:` to 10m, or bump thresholds by ~20% depending on model sequence length. Also add a short suppression window during deploys. Typical workflow: deploy tuned rule to staging for 48h evaluation then promote.

devon: Note I changed the tenant rule naming to include model so it's easier to filter: `tenant_latency_<model>`. Will roll the change in tonight's release — heads up if you pin any rule names.

alex.p: Network notes:
- OTLP ingestion: outbound HTTPS to ingest.private.redwood (443). We terminate OTLP at our edge (4318/4317 internally).
- If we deploy Prom/Grafana in-customer: inbound traffic only inside peered VPCs; ports: node-exporter 9100, custom app metrics default 9102, grafana 3000 (but proxied/443 in console).
- If customer wants us to scrape their Prometheus over peering, they must open 9100/9102 from our scraper IPs and set up auth if required.

observability-bot: Checklist created: https://internal.redwood.dev/checklists/private-observability — items: helm values template, tenant-id, grafana user invite, alert tuning checklist, network security review.

sara.m: Perfect. Can you drop a sample dashboard for p99 latency and KV cache hit rate? If we have that JSON I can share with the customer. Thanks :thumbsup:

mike.r: I have a lightweight p99+cache dashboard template. Will open a PR to dashboards/acme-p99-cache.json — ping me if you want it tweaked.

devon: If you need Grafana user created in managed-per-tenant, go to Private Deployments -> acme-privacy -> Observability -> Invite (console). For self-hosted grafana we provide an admin kube secret with initial credentials.

sara.m: OK. I'll follow the helm path and ask for the sample dashboard. Thanks all, closing loop unless anything else comes up.

mike.r: Ping me for a quick PR review.

observability-bot: Reminder: schedule network security review for peering if pulling metrics across accounts.

sara.m: Will do — marking this thread done once grafana/dashboard PR is merged.
